The latest figure is 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 living in poverty in 2024. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line, on its 2023 base. It comes from Statistics Canada's Canadian Income Survey, released 2026-04-29.

- **Number of children:** about 135,500 in 2024.
- **Recent trend:** 12.0% in 2022 and 11.9% in 2023. It was 8.1% in 2021, though StatCan's status code for that year is different from 2022–2024 and I didn't check what it means.
- **Average gap ratio:** 26.9% in 2024. This is how far, on average, a poor child's family income falls below the poverty line.
- **Other measures:** the same table also gives rates on the Low Income Measure and the Low Income Cut-offs. These give different rates, and I didn't pull them.

Canada's real GDP grew about **3.3% at an annualized rate** in Q2 2026 (April–June). That is up from 0.1% quarterly growth in Q1 2026.

I calculated this from the seasonally adjusted chained (2017) dollar levels. GDP rose from $2,503,604 million in Q1 to $2,524,127 million in Q2, which is 0.82% for the quarter. Compounding that over four quarters gives 3.3%.

Statistics Canada's percent-change series (v1594571783, "Seasonally adjusted at annual rates") shows 0.8% for Q2. That figure is the quarter-over-quarter change, even though the series title says "annual rates", so it is not the annualized rate. Statistics Canada's headline annualized figure may differ slightly from mine because of rounding.

The data were released 2026-08-28.

I haven't checked this against CMHC's current methodology page, so treat the wording as a paraphrase from memory.

- **Absorbed:** In the Market Absorption Survey, a newly completed unit counts as absorbed once it is no longer available on the market. For a unit built for sale (condominium or freehold), that means a buyer has bought it. For a rental unit, it means a tenant has leased it. The survey tracks units from completion until they are absorbed. It reports the share of completed units absorbed and the number still unabsorbed.
- **Sold:** CMHC treats a unit as sold when there is a binding purchase contract, usually with a deposit paid. It does not need to be closed or occupied. A reservation or a letter of intent is not a sale.

I haven't confirmed the exact conditions CMHC attaches to a sale, such as whether any conditions must be removed. Check the survey's "Methodology" or "Definitions" page on cmhc-schl.gc.ca for the exact text.

CMHC conducts the Rental Market Survey every year in October. Some collection can run into early November. CMHC publishes the results in the following months, usually in December.

The survey covers privately initiated rental structures with at least three units:
- **Apartments:** purpose-built rental apartment buildings with three or more units.
- **Row (townhouse) structures:** rental row houses with three or more units.

It covers urban centres with a population of 10,000 or more. It doesn't cover condominium units rented out individually or secondary rentals such as basement suites, single-family homes and duplexes. It also excludes social and subsidized housing.

I answered this from my knowledge of CMHC's published methodology and didn't check it against the live CMHC page today. The unit-count threshold and the population cutoff are the details most worth confirming there.

I couldn't check the marketed status of DIN 02471477, so I can't say whether that Ozempic pen is currently marketed in Canada.

The Drug Product Database (DPD) is on the Open Government portal as "Drug Product Database – All Files". None of its resources are loaded into the portal's queryable DataStore. The record for a DIN is only available through Health Canada's live API or the DPD web search. My tools can't reach either one.

You can check it yourself in either of these ways:
- **Web search:** search DIN 02471477 in the DPD at canada.ca. The "Status" field shows "Marketed" if it is on the market.
- **API:** `https://health-products.canada.ca/api/drug/drugproduct/?din=02471477&lang=en&type=json` returns the product's status, and `https://health-products.canada.ca/api/drug/status/?id=<drug_code>&lang=en&type=json` returns the status for a given `drug_code`.
